newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Premium buying dominate activity in FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Premium buying dominate activity in FTSE.

text.p: Uncertainties about direction of the UK stock market kept many options traders away on Tuesday and the main deals were from players expecting the market to weaken over the next few months, dealers said.
Put options in the FTSE 100 index were bought as the market struggled to go higher.
One of the larger deals was from a buyer of 3,000 September 4325 puts in European style FTSE at 12-1/2p. Another was to buy 1,200 December 4925 puts at about 191p.
For a profit, both deals rely on FTSE futures to fall sufficiently before the options expire.
In contrast, one of the larger deals in stock options was the purchase of 500 October 160 calls in British Steel at 11-1/2p, which will make money if the underlying shares go up.
By 1335 GMT, cash FTSE had slipped back 0.7 at 4861.9, while September FTSE futures were down 20 points to 4856 and British Steel shares gained 2-1/2p to 161-1/4p.
